pages.text:
# Expert layer: `conatus.expert`

```python
import conatus.expert as ex          # or: from conatus.expert import *
```

Use the expert layer to write a spectral problem term by term (bases, tau variables and lifts
chosen by hand), to reach options the native layer does not expose, or to use a tool that the
native API does not offer on `m.compile(N).problem` or `sim.solver`. It is the representation
that native models compile to.

A name reachable in both layers means the same thing in both: the same object, or, for
`discretize`, `linearize`, `methods` and `verify`, the package `cn.<name>` whose call is the
function `conatus.expert.<name>` (`cn.discretize(problem)` works; `cn.discretize.Plan` too).
`conatus.api` is the former name of the expert layer: it still works, with a `FutureWarning`, and
will be removed. Two names keep their former meaning only there: `sensitivity` (now the package
`conatus.sensitivity`; the dense-eigenproblem helper is `conatus.solvers.sensitivity`) and
`Channel` (now `ChannelBaseFlow`; `cn.Channel` is the native geometry).

`conatus.expert` re-exports, under their own names, the public objects of the user-facing modules
that this documentation shows. Since 0.1.1 the list is reviewed name by name. A helper, a constant
or a result type that no page shows stays in its module (`conatus.contour.box`,
`conatus.timestep.rk_tableau`). Written as `conatus.expert.<name>`, such a name
raises an `AttributeError` that names the module (since 0.3). Every exception and
warning class of `conatus.errors` is exported (each has its entry in {doc}`../guide/errors`).

The Studio's telemetry recorder and wire protocol are not part of the expert layer. Import them as
`conatus.telemetry`. The modules themselves stay reachable as attributes (`conatus.expert.ecs`,
`conatus.expert.provenance`), but their canonical name is `conatus.<module>`.
`conatus.expert.explain()` lists the name clashes and how each one is handled:

- two modules export different objects under the same name: the first one is kept, the other stays
  reachable as `conatus.<module>.<name>`;
- a name with two unrelated meanings is not exported at all: `record` is refused
  (`AmbiguousNameError`); the run provenance record is exported as `provenance_record`, and the
  telemetry frame is `conatus.telemetry.record`;
- an object named like a module (`linearize`, `discretize`, `methods`): the module stays
  `conatus.<module>`, callable as the function;
- generic helpers stay in their module; the run registry is a module, `conatus.expert.runs`
  (= `cn.runs`). The compiled runtime and the MPI backend are left out of the single import.

```{eval-rst}
.. autofunction:: conatus.expert.explain
```

```{toctree}
:maxdepth: 1

_generated/reference
```

pages.text:
# API reference

Conatus has two layers. Most scripts only need the first.

- **The user layer**, `import conatus as cn`: named geometries (`cn.Box`, `cn.Channel`, `cn.Disk`,
  …), the model in which equations are written as on paper (`cn.Model`), the objects it returns
  (simulation, linearisation, compiled problem), and the utilities (`cn.problems`, `cn.runs`,
  `cn.doctor()`, `cn.from_dedalus`, `cn.parse_equation`). See {doc}`user`.
- **The expert layer**, `conatus.expert`: the mathematical intermediate representation (fields,
  bases, operators, problems written term by term) and every toolkit that works on it (solvers,
  time stepping, adjoints, invariant solutions, continuation, bifurcations, Floquet–Hill,
  non-modal analysis, chaos, data-driven methods, provenance). See {doc}`expert`. The Studio's
  telemetry recorder is a separate module, `conatus.telemetry`.

The two layers meet in one place: `m.compile(N).problem` is an ordinary expert-layer problem, and
`sim.solver` is an ordinary expert-layer time stepper. Pass them to the tools that support their
geometry and scheme; each tool's page states its scope.

```{toctree}
:maxdepth: 2

user
expert
```

# User layer: `import conatus as cn`

```python
import conatus as cn
```

`import conatus` loads the solvers, the compiled core and the GPU modules only when they are first
used.
The names below are reached as `cn.<name>`.

## Geometries

A geometry fixes the coordinates, the spectral bases (chosen once per geometry, printed by
`explain()`) and the names of the boundaries used by {meth}`Model.at <conatus.Model.at>`.

```{eval-rst}
.. currentmodule:: conatus

.. autosummary::
   :toctree: _generated/user
   :nosignatures:

   Box
   Channel
   Disk
   Annulus
   Pipe
   Sphere
   Ball
   Shell
   TaylorCouette
   MappedBox
   periodic
   walls
   line
   half_line
   between
```

`cn.Cylinder` is another name for `cn.Pipe`.

## Wall conditions on a vector unknown

Named conditions for `m.at(...)` (guide: {doc}`../guide/boundary_conditions`).

```{eval-rst}

.. autosummary::
   :toctree: _generated/user
   :nosignatures:

   Simulation
   Linearization
   Compiled
```

## Ready problems: `cn.problems`

Canonical flows written once, each returning an ordinary problem with its handles and the
reference it reproduces.

```{eval-rst}

```

## The run registry: `cn.runs`

Record runs, find and compare them, reproduce one bit for bit (guide: {doc}`../guide/runs`).

```{eval-rst}

.. autosummary::
   :toctree: _generated/user

   record
   find
   get
   compare
   lineage
   reproduce
   to_dataframe
   export
   explain
   Run
   RunList
   Registry
```

## Quantities of a run

Series, spectra and profiles of a simulation, what to watch while it runs, and the statistics of a
result (guide: {doc}`../guide/diagnostics`).

```{eval-rst}
.. currentmodule:: conatus

.. autosummary::
   :toctree: _generated/user
   :nosignatures:

   series
   spectrum
   profile
   view
   time_average
   uncertainty
   StopRun
```

`cn.StopRun` is the exception a callback raises to stop a run.

## Utilities

```{eval-rst}
.. currentmodule:: conatus

.. autosummary::
   :toctree: _generated/user
   :nosignatures:

   doctor
   from_dedalus
   parse_equation
   parse_expr
```

## Regions of the complex plane: `cn.box`, `cn.contour`

`m.eigenvalues(N, ..., region=cn.box(re=(a, b), im=(c, d)))` returns the eigenvalues in the box,
with a count estimated by the argument principle from samples of the determinant on the boundary.
`cn.contour.count` and `cn.contour.beyn` take any operator
({doc}`../guide/dynamics/contour`).

pages.text:
# Citing Conatus

If Conatus contributes to your work, please cite the software. The repository carries a
`CITATION.cff` file (GitHub shows it as "Cite this repository"); the same entry in BibTeX:

```bibtex
@software{dahan2026conatus,
  author  = {Dahan, Ruben},
  title   = {{Conatus: spectral PDEs and dynamical systems}},
  year    = {2026},
  version = {0.3.0},
  license = {BSD-3-Clause},
  url     = {https://github.com/rubendahan/conatus},
}
```

A paper describing the design and the validation tests is in preparation.

## Cite the methods too

Conatus implements published methods; please cite them along with Conatus. `plan.methods()`
drafts a *Methods* paragraph for your run and returns the BibTeX entries of the methods it cites
(for example Olver & Townsend 2013 for the
ultraspherical operators, Burns et al. 2020 for the generalised tau method, Vasil et al. 2016 and
2019 for polar and spherical bases, Ascher, Ruuth & Spiteri 1997 for the IMEX Runge–Kutta
schemes). See {doc}`guide/explain`.

## Validation references

The published values reproduced by the tutorials and the gallery are listed on each page with
their source. When you use Conatus to reproduce or extend one of them, cite the original work.

pages.text:
# For AI agents

What an AI coding agent reads before using Conatus, and the JSON interface it uses while it works.

An agent that writes and runs Conatus code should be given one page,
`AGENTS.md`, at the root of the repository and of this website (`/AGENTS.md`, with `/llms.txt`
for tools that look for it). It lists the usable surface, one call per line, grouped by task. It
also gives rules against common agent mistakes: read a refusal and its suggested fix, write each
tolerance that decides digits, check residuals, convergence and `explain()`, and check cost and
memory before a large run. The test suite checks the page against the library: the names it cites
exist, the major public elements are listed, and its example runs.

## Ask the library, in JSON

Three commands answer an agent without any prose to parse. Each prints one JSON object (keys
sorted, `"api": 1`; within an API version fields are only added) and says what happened by its
exit code.

```bash
python -m conatus agent                          # versions, CPU/GPU, the user layer, watched runs
python -m conatus agent explain cn.Model.simulate     # signature, required arguments and tolerances
                                                      # (and "deprecated": former argument names)
python -m conatus agent explain cn.problems.native.rayleigh_benard   # a ready model: its unknowns too
python -m conatus agent check run.py             # dry run of a script: what Conatus would refuse
```

`check` runs the script for real up to its first expensive call (a time integration, an
eigenvalue solve, a Newton search, a continuation…) and stops there. On the way, `simulate` builds
its solver, so a search that takes `sim.solver` is reached too; calls that write files or announce
a Studio run (`watch`, `output`, `checkpoints`, `save`) are skipped. At the stop, the call's
arguments are checked against its signature, the model is discretised at the requested resolution
(so an under-resolved coefficient or a missing boundary condition is refused here, with its fix),
and the `explain()` texts are collected. With `backend="cuda"`, `simulate` itself is the stop (no
device memory is allocated) and the device memory of the simulation is predicted; `--memory` does
the same prediction for a CPU simulation. No intercepted call integrates or solves (the list is
`conatus.agent.EXPENSIVE`).

The argument values of the stopped call are checked only where the call has a separate check
that does nothing else: `Simulation.run` and `IVPSolver.run` (a negative or fractional number of
steps, an end time before the clock, a callback without `every`). For any other stop, a value the
call would refuse (a negative tolerance, a bracket in the wrong order) is found only when the
script runs. The `validated` field of the report says, for the stop, which of the two applied, and
`ok` means that nothing was refused among the checks that ran.

`check` is not a sandbox. The script runs in the current process with your privileges: its own
code (writing a file, starting a subprocess) runs as written, and only the Conatus calls of that
list are intercepted, in that process only (not in a child process or an MPI launch). A script
that catches the stop (a bare `except:` or `except BaseException`) and goes on is reported as an
error, since the lines after it ran for real. The timeout cannot interrupt a long call inside
compiled code. Check only scripts you would run yourself.

For this script, where the drift test of an eigenvalue solve was asked for without its tolerance,

```python
import conatus as cn

m = cn.Model(cn.Box(y=cn.walls(-1, 1)), name="Orr-Sommerfeld", Re=1e4, alpha=1.0)
m.scalar("v")
m.given(U=lambda y: 1 - y**2)
m.eigenvalue("c", growth="imag")
m.define("L2(f) = dy(dy(f)) - alpha**2*f")
m.equations("L2(L2(v))/(1j*alpha*Re) - U*L2(v) + dy(dy(U))*v + c*L2(v) = 0")
m.at("walls", "v = 0", "dy(v) = 0")
res = m.eigenvalues(N=64, drift=96)          # drift test without its tolerance
```

the report says what is missing, where, and the value Conatus suggests (exit code 1):

```json
{
 "api": 1,
 "calls": [
  {
   "action": "stopped",
   "call": "Model.eigenvalues",
   "line": 10
  }
 ],
 "command": "check",
 "errors": [],
 "explain": {
  "model": "Model 'Orr-Sommerfeld' ...",
  "plan": "Discretization plan for EVP 'Orr-Sommerfeld' ..."
 },
 "memory": null,
 "missing": [
  {
   "argument": "drift_tol",
   "call": "Model.eigenvalues",
   "kind": "tolerance",
   "suggest": "1e-6",
   "when": "drift=N2"
  }
 ],
 "notes": [],
 "ok": false,
 "plan": {
  "groups": 1,
  "type": "Plan"
 },
 "refusals": [],
 "script": "os_check.py",
 "stopped_at": {
  "call": "Model.eigenvalues",
  "line": 10
 },
 "validated": [
  {
   "call": "Model.eigenvalues",
   "checked": "signature, conditional tolerances and discretization; the argument values are checked only when the call runs",
   "values": "not checked"
  }
 ],
 "warnings": []
}
```

| exit code | `agent info` / `explain` / `check` |
|---|---|
| 0 | done; for `check`, nothing refused or missing |
| 1 | `check`: a refusal, a missing argument or tolerance, or an error in the script |
| 2 | usage error; `explain FILE.py` (explain does not run a script: use `check`) |
| 4 | `explain`: no such public name |

The same functions are available from Python: `conatus.agent.info()`, `conatus.agent.describe(name)`
and `conatus.agent.check(path)` return the dictionaries printed above.

## Follow a run that is already going

A long run declared with `sim.watch(...)` is followed and piloted with
`python -m conatus studio status|watch|send|frame|log`, with its own exit codes and per-agent
tokens: see {doc}`studio_agents`.

## AGENTS.md

The start of the page, as an agent reads it: installation, the mental model, a working example,
the surface by task and the rules. The rest of
[`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/rubendahan/conatus/blob/main/AGENTS.md) covers live runs
({doc}`studio_agents`) and the JSON contract described above.

# AGENTS.md — Conatus for AI agents (read before writing any Conatus code)

Conatus: spectral PDEs and dynamical systems on CPU and GPU (0.2; the API is young, see the deprecation notes below).
You write equations as on paper; Conatus discretises (Fourier/Chebyshev/curvilinear bases, taus
placed for you), integrates, solves eigenproblems and finds structure (orbits, bifurcations, Floquet, optimal perturbations).
Declare numerical choices explicitly. When a call lacks one, Conatus raises an error that says what to write.
A few older inferences remain (the growth convention of an eigenvalue) and emit a `DefaultChoiceWarning`.

## 1. Install, verify, orient (machine-readable)

```bash
pip install ".[tutorials]"             # or installed (Python 3.11-3.13; h5py + matplotlib); writes only under ~/.cache/conatus
python -m conatus doctor --json        # what this machine can run; exit 1 if something required is missing
python -m conatus agent                # JSON: versions, CPU/GPU, user-layer names, watched runs
python -m conatus agent explain cn.Model.simulate     # signature, required args, required tolerances (+ unknowns of a ready model)
python -m conatus agent check run.py   # dry run (no solve): refusals + fix, missing tolerances, memory
```

## 2. Mental model

- `import conatus as cn`: **native layer**. Geometry → `cn.Model` (unknowns, parameters, equations
  as text, conditions by boundary name) → numerics given at the call (`N`, `scheme`, `dt`,
  `backend`) → result object with `.explain()`.
- `import conatus.expert as X`: **expert layer** (IR: bases, fields, `X.IVP`/`X.EVP`/…,
  `X.discretize` → `X.Plan`, `X.IVPSolver`). Every model compiles to it: `m.compile(N).problem`,
  `sim.solver`, `sim.plan`. A name present in both layers has one meaning.
- One word per notion: `steps` (number of time steps), `k` (a wavenumber keyword; a problem
  parameter keeps its literature name, e.g. `alpha` of Orr–Sommerfeld), `eta` (radius
  ratio), `n_modes`, `max_iterations`, `tol` (exceptions: the fields `ContinuationSettings(tolerance=, max_newton=)`, also read as `cfg.tol`, `cfg.max_iterations`);
  former names warn (`conatus._deprecation.RENAMES`).
- Names below: `m` = `cn.Model`, `sim` = `cn.model.Simulation`, `lin` = `cn.model.Linearization`, `X` = `conatus.expert`.

## 3. Minimal working example (executed by the test suite)

```python
import numpy as np
import conatus as cn

m = cn.Model(cn.Box(x=cn.periodic(22.0)), name="Kuramoto-Sivashinsky")
m.scalar("u")
m.equations("dt(u) + lap(u) + lap(lap(u)) = -u*dx(u)")
sim = m.simulate(N=32, scheme="RK443", dt=0.01)        # N, scheme and dt are required
sim.initial(u=lambda x: np.cos(2 * np.pi * x / 22.0))
sim.run(steps=20)                                     # run(until=T) must land on a whole step
print(sim.explain())                                  # short summary; full=True adds compiler decisions

os_ = cn.Model(cn.Box(y=cn.walls(-1, 1)), name="Orr-Sommerfeld", Re=1e4, alpha=1.0)
os_.scalar("v")
os_.given(U=lambda y: 1 - y**2)
os_.eigenvalue("c", growth="imag")
os_.define("L2(f) = dy(dy(f)) - alpha**2*f")
os_.equations("L2(L2(v))/(1j*alpha*Re) - U*L2(v) + dy(dy(U))*v + c*L2(v) = 0")
os_.at("walls", "v = 0", "dy(v) = 0")
res = os_.eigenvalues(N=64, drift=96, drift_tol=1e-6)  # drift test removes modes that move with N
i = int(res.order()[0])                               # least stable first (growth = Im c)
assert res.residuals[i] < 1e-12                       # check the residual (then convergence in N)
```

Critical point of a ready linearization, and its mode (Rayleigh–Bénard, no-slip walls):

```python
import numpy as np
import conatus as cn
import conatus.expert as X

lin = cn.problems.native.rayleigh_benard_evp(k=3.1, Ra=1708.0, Pr=1.0)
P = lin.parametric(24, over=("Ra", "k"), drift=32, drift_tol=1e-6)   # k: the wavenumber
crit = X.critical(P, "Ra", bracket=(1500.0, 2000.0), over={"k": (2.5, 3.8)}, xtol=1e-9)
assert abs(crit.value - 1707.762) < 1e-3 and abs(crit.over["k"] - 3.1163) < 1e-3
kc = crit.over["k"]
res = cn.problems.native.rayleigh_benard_evp(k=kc, Ra=crit.value, Pr=1.0).eigenvalues(
    24, k=kc, drift=32, drift_tol=1e-6)
md = res.mode(int(res.order()[0]))
T = md.at("T", z=np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 101))[0]     # walls included; row x = 0
```

## 4. The surface, by task (one minimal call each)

| Task | Call |
|---|---|
| Geometries | `cn.Box(x=cn.periodic(L), z=cn.walls(a, b))`, `cn.Channel(Lx, Lz)`, `cn.Disk(R)`, `cn.Annulus(ri, ro)`, `cn.Pipe(R, L)` (= `cn.Cylinder`), `cn.TaylorCouette(ri, ro, L)`, `cn.Sphere(R)`, `cn.Ball(R)`, `cn.Shell(ri, ro)`, `cn.MappedBox(x=cn.periodic(L), z=cn.between(b, t))` (wavy walls, `b`/`t` numbers or `lambda x: ...`) |
| Axes | `cn.periodic(L, complex=False)`, `cn.walls(a, b)`, `cn.walls(a, c, b)` (compound: its entry of `N` is a tuple `(N1, N2)`), `cn.walls(a, b, basis="sincos")`, `cn.half_line(0, scale=s)`, `cn.line(0, scale=s)` (`scale` required) |
| Unknowns, data | `m.velocity("u")`, `m.pressure("p")` (also the pressure of a normal-mode model on one wall axis: `1j*k*p`, `dz(p)`), `m.scalar("T")`, `m.vector("B")`, `m.given(U=lambda y: ...)`, `m.eigenvalue("c", growth="imag")` (declare how a mode grows: `"real"` for exp(s t), `"imag"` for a phase speed; left out: v0.1 guesses from the name with a `DefaultChoiceWarning`), `m.define("L2(f) = ...")`, `m.function("g", f, derivative=df)` |
| Equations | `m.equations("dt(u) + grad(p) - lap(u)/Re = -u·grad(u)", "div(u) = 0")`; ops `dt dx..dz grad div lap curl integ interp`, `·`/`@` dot; override split with `explicit(...)`/`implicit(...)`; `cross(ez, u)` (Cartesian frame e_x x e_y = e_z; with a constant vector on the left-hand side it is implicit, e.g. Coriolis `2*Om*cross(ez, u)`: stable at any dt but its waves are damped when |W| dt > 1 — `explain()` gives |W| dt, `UnderResolvedWarning` above 1); parse only: `cn.parse_equation`, `cn.parse_expr` |
| Boundary conditions | `m.at("bottom", u=0, T=1)`, `m.at("walls", "v = 0", "dy(v) = 0")`, `m.at("top", u=cn.free_slip)`, `cn.no_slip`, `cn.navier_slip(l)`, time-dependent `m.at("top", u="cos(t)")`; force a tau target: `into=` |
| Inspect before running | `m.explain(N)`, `m.compile(N)` (`.problem`, `.fields`, `.decisions()`), `m.discretize(N)` → `X.Plan` (`.explain()`, `.rank_report()`, `.check()`); same with `lin.compile(N)`, `lin.discretize(N, k=k)`, `lin.explain(N)`, `lin.group(plan, k)` |
| Expert problems | `X.IVP`, `X.EVP`, `X.LBVP`, `X.NLBVP` (`add_equation("...")`, `add_bc`), `X.discretize(problem, ncc=)` = `cn.discretize`, `X.IVPSolver(plan, "RK443", dt)` (`sim.solver`), `X.CFL`, `X.EmbeddedError`, `X.TauWatch`; `cn.linearize` (IR linearisation), `cn.model`, `cn.expert`, `cn.translate` |
| Parameters | `m.<name> = value` (e.g. Ra) or `m.params["Ra"] = 1e5` (declared names only, validated; the next compile uses it); for one call: `m.simulate(N, ..., Ra=3000)` (also `eigenvalues`, `solve`, `discretize`; printed by `sim.explain()`) |
| Create a simulation | `sim = m.simulate(N, scheme="RK443", dt=1e-3, backend="cpu")` (schemes: `X.SCHEMES`; a NaN or inf stops the run with `cn.errors.NumericalError`, checked every 100 steps by default, `check_finite=` to change it) |
| Initial state | `sim.initial(T=f)` (`f` a callable, a number, or an array shaped as `sim.grid("T")`); `t=t0` starts the clock at `t0`, and forcing, boundary data, outputs and checkpoints use that clock |
| Advance | `sim.run(until=T)`, `sim.run(steps=n, callback=f, every=k)`, `sim.cfl("u", safety=0.5)`, `sim.dt` |
| Inspect the state | `sim.t`, `sim.iteration`, `sim.grid("T")`, `sim.coordinate("z")`, `sim.coeffs("T")`, `sim.evaluate("dz(T)")` (`"integ(T)"` gives a number), `sim.properties(every=k, ...)` |
| Boundary-value | `m.solve(N)` (LBVP); nonlinear: `X.NewtonSolver(m.compile(N).problem, tol=1e-10)` `.solve(guess)` (`damping=1.0`, `max_iterations=50` defaulted, printed) |
| Eigenvalues | `res = m.eigenvalues(N, drift=N2, drift_tol=1e-6)` → `.values`, `.residuals`, `.explain()`, `res.order()` (least stable first by the growth convention); `left=True` for adjoint modes; expert `X.eigenvalues(plan, drift_plan=plan2, drift_tol=1e-6)` |
| Eigenmodes | `md = res.mode(i)` → `md["v"]` (complex grid values, taus left out, declared normalisation), `md.coordinate("y")`, `md.at("v", y=pts)` (walls included) |
| Spurious and unresolved modes | `drift=` compares two resolutions and removes modes that move (`drift` > N, `drift_tol` in (0, 1e-2]; if every mode is removed, `ResolutionError`). A spectral-tail test, on by default, flags modes whose energy sits in the last coefficients (`res.flagged`, ranked last by `order()`; `spurious="none"` turns it off). Without `drift=`, a selected mode above `cn.tolerances.UNRESOLVED_TAIL_TOL` (1e-10) gives a `ResolutionWarning`: raise N or pass `drift=` |
| Periodic axes, linearizations | `m.eigenvalues(N, k=wavenumber)` on a model with a periodic axis (without `k` it is refused: name the group); `n_modes=` counts shift-invert modes; curvilinear: `m=`, `kz=`, `ell=`. `lin = m.linearize(about={u: 0, T: lambda z: -z})`, `lin.eigenvalues(N, k=kx)`; a base that is not steady is refused unless `base_residual="accept"` |
| Eigenvalues in a region | `res = m.eigenvalues(N, region=cn.box(re=(a, b), im=(c, d)))` → every eigenvalue in the box, `res.count` (counted by the argument principle from samples of the determinant on the boundary; refused when the sampling checks fail or an eigenvalue sits on the boundary), `res.count_method`, `res.multiplicity`; any operator: `cn.contour.count(T, box)` (`T` = `(L, M)`, a `HillBlocks` or `z -> T(z)` with `poles=`), `cn.contour.beyn(T, box, poles=0, derivative=dT)` (nonlinear `T(z) v = 0`, roots accepted at residual `<= 1e-13` by default) |
| Parametric, thresholds | `P = m.parametric(N, over=("Re", "alpha"), drift=N2, drift_tol=1e-6)` (drift: modes that move between resolutions are removed); ready linearizations: `lin.parametric(N, over=("Ra", "k"), drift=N2, drift_tol=1e-6)` (`k` = the wavenumber, `lin.wavenumber_names()`), `X.critical(P, "Re", bracket=(a, b), xtol=1e-9)` (the growth must change sign between `a` and `b`: checked at both ends, else refused with the sub-brackets where it does; a neutral curve can have two branches, e.g. Orr–Sommerfeld at alpha = 1 between Re = 5000 and 40000: bracket each; growth from the eigenvalue's declaration `m.eigenvalue("c", growth="imag")`, `lin`: Re s; only modes passing the spectral-tail test are selected; without a drift pencil the tail of the critical mode is printed and an under-resolved one warns (`crit.unresolved_note`); missing parameters take the model's values), `P.least_stable(...)`, `P.track(...)`, `P.sensitivity(mode, "Re")` |
| Transient growth | `lin.optimal_gain(N, k=k, t0=0, T=T, steps=n, scheme="RK443")` → `.G`; `X.max_growth(ss, (t1, t2), xtol=)` (`n_scan=64` declared default), `X.optimal_growth`, `conatus.growth.growth_at` |
| Floquet / Hill (periodic base) | `m.linearize(about={u: base(y, t)}, period=1.0)`, `lin.floquet(N, k=k, method="hill", Nh=16, targets=[0.0], tol=1e-12)` (`fl.harmonic_tails`; a leading mode with more than `cn.tolerances.HILL_TAIL_TOL` of its weight in the outermost harmonics warns "truncated in Nh": raise Nh) or `method="monodromy", steps=, scheme=`; `lin.harmonics`, `lin.periodic_operator(N, k=k)`; `X.HillBlocks`, `X.shell_floquet` |
| Invariant solutions (ECS) | `nk = X.NewtonKrylovHookstep(tol=1e-12)` (algorithm controls defaulted, printed; trust radii absolute by default, `radii="relative"` for states far from norm 1); **1D periodic problems only** (one real Fourier axis, e.g. KS): `X.find_equilibrium(sim, x0, nk)` (odd subspace), `X.find_travelling_wave(sim, x0, c0, nk)`, `X.find_relative_periodic_orbit(sim, x0, T0, ell0, nk, steps=)`; the seed `x0`: `sim.grid("u")` (grid values, converted and declared in the notes), the simulation itself (its current state) or the state vector `sim.solver.X`; a search converges only from a seed near the solution (most seeds of a chaotic run fall back to an equilibrium or fail: tutorial 5); walls / 2D / 3D: `conatus.ecs.steady.AffineSteadyProblem`, `conatus.ecs.pipe.PipeTravellingWave`; stability `X.equilibrium_eigenvalues(sim, tw, n_modes, arnoldi_tol=1e-12)`, `X.floquet_multipliers(sim, rpo, n_modes, arnoldi_tol=1e-12)` (a `Simulation` or its solver, as the finders); edge: `X.EdgeTracker`, `X.ThresholdBisection` |
| Continuation, bifurcation | `X.ContinuationSettings(ds=, ds_min=, ds_max=, tolerance=, max_points=)` (`adapt`, `fast_iterations`, `max_newton`, `dp_fd="auto"` defaulted), `X.NLBVPContinuation(newton, "lam", settings).run(...)`, `X.continue_equilibria(X.ir_system(X.ode_problem(...), ["r"]), x0, "r", cfg, marginal_tol=)`, `X.continue_orbits`, `X.branch_switch`, `X.normal_form`, `X.continue_codim2` |
| Manifolds, slices, chaos | `X.ecs_system(sim.solver, odd=, degree=, dense_max=)`, `X.unstable_manifold`, `X.FirstFourierModeSlice`, `X.lyapunov_spectrum`, `X.Ensemble`, `X.ensemble_fate`, `X.poincare_section` |
| Lyapunov, covariant vectors | `res = sim.lyapunov(k, transient=, align=, T=, reortho_every=10, inner="euclidean", n_blocks=, seed=, starts=[{...}], zero_mean="u", covariant=True, clv_window=, clv_backward=, clv_checkpoints=s)` (durations must be whole numbers of steps and intervals; the tangent is that of the discrete step) → `res.exponents`, `res.stderr`, `res.kaplan_yorke()`, `res.clv`, `res.clv_grid("u", i)`, `res.angles(j)`, `res.pair_angle(i, j)`, `res.domination(tau)` (`.clusters`, `.n_physical`, `.violation(j)`), `res.clv_covariance_residual` |
| Particles, dye | `pt = sim.particles(X0, path=, every=, velocity="u", at_walls="refuse")` (velocity evaluated from the spectral coefficients at the points, RK4 per step: order 4 steady, 3 unsteady; `"clip"` puts wall-crossers back, counted) → `pt.positions(unwrapped=True)`, `pt.velocities()`; `m.dye("c", velocity="u", kappa=1e-3)` (conservative form, no-flux walls; `kappa=0`: conservative advection only), `sim.dye("c", path, every=)` (mass, variance, min, max, tail) |
| Adjoint, optimal perturbations | `fm = sim.flowmap(T, t0=, checkpoints=)` → `fm.jvp`, `fm.vjp` (dot-product test; on a shell with `f_backend="fused"` the vjp follows the planned path, `fm.explain()` says which equations); `nl = sim.nlop(T=, E0=, t0=)`, `nl.linear_gain(n_modes=1, tol=1e-12)`; long reverse sweeps over several jobs: `X.FlowMap(..., checkpoint_store="disk").vjp(X0, W, journal=, budget_s=)` raises `X.VJPSuspended`, resume with `fm.vjp(X0, None, journal=)`; `X.compare_adjoints`, `X.structural_sensitivity` |
| Symmetry | native parities: `cn.walls(a, b, basis="sincos")` (parity read from the BCs); expert `X.SymmetrySubspace(X.Reflection(x), u=X.EVEN, T=X.ODD)`; check what a subspace hides: `X.symmetry_breaking_check` |
| GPU, distributed | install: `docs/site/install.md` (GPU section, tested CUDA 12.9 / CuPy 14.2); `m.simulate(..., backend="cuda", f_backend="fused")`, `X.gpu_available()`, `X.gpu_report()` |
| Memory, cost | `conatus.runtime.memory.plan_memory(plan, "RK443")` (device memory before any GPU), `conatus.runtime.memory.memory_report(sim.solver)` (CUDA solvers; totals include the declared CUDA process floor `CUDA_PROCESS_FLOOR_BYTES`); `python -m conatus agent check run.py --memory` |
| Resolution | `sim.plan.resolution_report(sim.solver, velocity="u")` → `.ok`, `.recommend()`; `cn.resolution.estimate_modes`; NCC options `ncc_cutoff=`, `ncc_tail_tol=` on any native call taking `N` |
| I/O, restart | `sim.output(path, tasks=["u"], every=50, mode="w")` (the state at the start is a row too: `initial=True` by default), `sim.checkpoints(dir, every=100)` (`keep=2` most recent by default), `sim.save(path)`, `sim.restart(cn.io.latest(dir))` (bit-for-bit; `latest` refuses a missing directory), `cn.io.read(path)` (`.to_xarray()`; every array has `dims` + HDF5 dimension scales; Cartesian 2D/3D outputs get a ParaView sidecar `<file>.xmf`, `cn.io.write_xdmf(path)`); one script for every job of a chain: `sim.resume_or_start(dir, T=f)` then `checkpoints`/`output` without `mode=` |
| Uncertainty | `cn.uncertainty(f, N=[8, 12, 16], dt=[0.04, 0.02, 0.01], scheme_order=2)` → `.value`, `.error`, `.trusted`; `cn.time_average(series, dt=, discard=)` |
| Data-driven | `X.dmd(X, dt=, rank=, inner_product=)` (amplitudes default `"first"`), `X.pod`, `X.spod`, `X.edmd`, `X.DataInnerProduct` |
| Ready problems | `cn.problems.native.rayleigh_benard(Lx=, Ra=, Pr=)` → `cn.Model` (start here; `cn.problems.<name>` of the same name is the expert `Ready`, resolution in the call) (also `channel`, `plane_couette`, `pipe`, `taylor_couette`, `kolmogorov`, `kuramoto_sivashinsky`, `swift_hohenberg`, `rotating_shell_convection`, `orr_sommerfeld`, `*_evp` → `lin`); expert `cn.problems` (`.problem`, `.ncc`, `.explain()`) |
| Provenance, runs | `sim.methods()` (Methods paragraph + BibTeX), `cn.methods`, `cn.verify`, `cn.runs.track(name)`, `cn.runs.find(...)`, `cn.runs.compare(a, b)`, `cn.runs.reproduce(run)` |
| Importing a Dedalus 3 script | `cn.from_dedalus("script.py")` (parsed, not executed) → `.explain()`, `.problem`, `.to_script()` |
| Studio (watch live) | `sim.watch("run_id", film={"T": cn.view("T")}, stats={...}, settable={"dt": (1e-4, 1e-2)}, every_s=0.5)` (periods in wall seconds: `every_s`, `scalars_every_s`, `controls_every_s`), `sim.unwatch()`; `cn.series(f)`, `cn.profile("T", "z")`, `cn.spectrum("u", "x")`; a Studio stop raises `cn.StopRun` in the run; limits and timings: `conatus.studio.constants.explain()` |
| Notebook, units | `cn.notebook`, `X.UnitSystem`, `X.convert`, `X.presets` |
| Errors, tolerances | `conatus.errors.explain()` (tree), `cn.errors`, `cn.tolerances.explain()` (every declared threshold), `cn.doctor()` |

## 5. Rules that prevent agent mistakes

1. **Errors carry a fix.** A refusal is a `cn.errors.ConatusError` with a stable `.error_code`, `.message`,
   `.where`, `.why`, `.fix`, `.doc` (and `.as_dict()`). Read `fix`, apply it yourself only if it is what you mean. Let numerical
   refusals propagate; if a script handles one, record the exception and the decision taken.
2. **Supply these accuracy arguments explicitly** (`REQUIRED`): `drift_tol`, `xtol` of
   `X.critical`, `tol` of `method="hill"` / `X.shell_floquet` / `nl.linear_gain` / `NewtonKrylovHookstep`,
   `tolerance` of `ContinuationSettings`, `tol` of `X.NewtonSolver`, `arnoldi_tol` of
   `X.equilibrium_eigenvalues` (required), `safety` of `sim.cfl` and of adaptive `X.EmbeddedError`.
   Write a value and say why; `agent explain <name>` lists them. Other accuracy defaults (for example the
   residual bound of `cn.contour.beyn`) are listed in the API reference of each call. Algorithm controls (trust radii,
   step growth, Krylov and iteration budgets, FD step) have declared defaults (`cn.tolerances.explain()`).
   Renamed arguments (`nmodes`/`k` → `n_modes`, `X0` → `x0`, `xatol` → `xtol`, `maxit` →
   `max_iterations`, `nsteps` → `steps`, `radius_ratio` → `eta`, ...) are refused since 0.3, and the message names the new one.
   When the answer may not be the one you meant, Conatus emits a `cn.errors.CorrectnessWarning`
   (`DefaultChoiceWarning`, for example). Python shows these by default, unlike a
   `DeprecationWarning`. Treat one as an error and declare the choice it names.
   Do not loosen a tolerance to make a refusal go away: find what is under-resolved.
3. **Under-resolved coefficients are refused** (non-constant coefficient tail > `cn.tolerances.NCC_TAIL_TOL`):
   raise `N`, or declare `ncc_cutoff=` / `ncc_tail_tol=` explicitly. Never truncate in your code.
   Callable initial data are refused when aliased, not periodic on a periodic axis or not finite,
   and warn (`cn.errors.InitialDataWarning`) when only not fully resolved (a coarse `N`);
   `initial(..., check=False)` only if you mean it; a run warns once
   (`cn.errors.UnderResolvedWarning`) when its spectral tail exceeds `RUN_TAIL_TOL`, and an
   ill-posed implicit term (backward diffusion) warns at compile (`cn.errors.IllPosedWarning`):
   treat both as errors in your script.
4. **Check results three ways**: the residual (`res.residuals`, `sol.residual`, `E1.residual`, `rank_report()`),
   convergence in `N` and `dt` (`resolution_report()`, `cn.uncertainty`), and an independent reference value
   when one exists. Report the value together with the checks you actually ran.
5. **Read `explain()`** of every object you report (`m`, `sim`, `res`, `lin`, plan): a short summary
   by default (problem, scheme, checks, warnings); `explain(full=True)` states bases,
   tau placement, implicit/explicit split, dealiasing (default (p+1)/2 for the highest polynomial
   degree p, at least 3/2: declared), filters, residuals.
6. `run(until=T)` must land on a whole number of steps (refused otherwise). `dt` stays fixed unless you
   build an adaptive controller. The CFL number limits the step for stability; it does not estimate the time error.
7. Restarts are bit-for-bit only with identical numerics (scheme, `dt`, `N`, options) and the same
   problem (model, equations, parameters, box): a mismatch is refused with the diff; a deliberate
   change is `sim.restart(path, allow=("kappa",))`. Use `sim.resume_or_start(dir, ...)` (or
   `cn.io.latest(dir)` + `sim.restart(...)`, which find `.h5` and `.npz`) for multi-job runs;
   both `.h5` and `.npz` restart bit for bit on CPU and GPU. Root searches raise when unconverged (`allow_unconverged=True` returns the
   flagged iterate); a Newton result with `trivial=True` is u = 0, not a new branch.
8. Cost first: `python -m conatus agent check run.py --memory` and `plan_memory` before a GPU job;
   `X.gpu_available()` before `backend="cuda"`. Small `N` on the CPU first, then scale. A second identical
   `m.simulate(...)` in the same process reuses the assembled operators (`sim.explain()` says "reused";
   any change of parameters, `N`, dealiasing, equations, conditions or data rebuilds them).
9. A solution found in a symmetry subspace is not declared stable until checked in the full space.
10. Transposed matrix ≠ physical adjoint; use `left=True`, `X.compare_adjoints`, `fm.vjp` as documented.
11. **Experimental (shipped and tested; may change without a deprecation cycle)**: the Studio,
    the local hub, shells larger than 64 × 48 × 48, 3-D channel and pipe
    orbits (`conatus.ecs.shooting.ShootingRPO`, `conatus.ecs.pipe.PipeTravellingWave`). First use warns `cn.errors.ExperimentalWarning`;
    say so in what you report. `X` exports documented names only: anything else is
    `conatus.<module>.<name>` (`X.<name>` is refused, and the refusal names the module).

## 6. Driving a run live (Studio channel, JSON, no server needed on a cluster)

```bash
python -m conatus studio runs                   # every run, live first (JSON, "api": 1)
python -m conatus studio status RUN             # state, t, iteration, dt, scalars, alerts, commands, settable
python -m conatus studio watch RUN --for 600    # one JSON line per change; always bounded
python -m conatus studio send RUN pause|resume|checkpoint
python -m conatus studio send RUN set dt=2e-3   # only if declared settable, within bounds
python -m conatus studio send RUN stop          # exit 5 + confirm_token; resend with --confirm TOKEN
python -m conatus studio log RUN -n 50 ; python -m conatus studio frame RUN --png out.png
```

Exit codes: 0 done (command written; confirm via events `command_received` → `param_set`/`set_refused`),
1 refused, 2 usage, 3 not authorised, 4 no such run, 5 confirmation needed, 6 hub unreachable.
Alerts: `non_finite`, `silent`, `set_refused`, `failed`, `log_errors`, … Act on one alert at a time,
check it was applied, then send the next command. Python: `from conatus.studio.client import connect`
(`cl.status`, `cl.send`, `cl.wait`). Hub tokens are per agent with a scope (`read` | `command`) and
run patterns (`python -m conatus.studio.hub --state DIR addagent NAME --scope command --runs 'host:kh_*' --token-out FILE`).
MCP client: `python -m conatus mcp` (extra `conatus[mcp]`), read-only unless started with `--allow COMMAND`;
run and record text arrives under `untrusted_data`. Guide: `guide/mcp`. Codes: `guide/error_codes`.
On a cluster: run agents and servers inside compute-node jobs, under the cluster's policy. Leave no background
process behind, and do not poll the scheduler in a loop.

## 7. `python -m conatus agent` — JSON contract (api 1; fields only added within a version)

- `info [--no-probe] [--no-runs]` → `api, command, conatus, python, platform, host, cpus, packages,
  gpu{probed, available, backend, cupy, core, visible_devices, how}, surface{cn, modules, expert}, runs{available, runs[]},
  commands, docs, rules`.
- `explain NAME` (`cn.<name>`, `expert.<name>`, `conatus.<module>.<name>`) → `qualified, kind, signature, summary, value, required,
  required_tolerances, conditional[{argument, when, suggest, kind}], deprecated{old: new},
  methods | names, explain`. Exit 4 if the name does not exist; `explain FILE.py` is refused
  (exit 2: it never runs a script, use `check`).
- `check SCRIPT.py [--memory] [--timeout S] [-- script args]` runs the script for real up to its
  first expensive call (a CPU `simulate` is built, a CUDA one stops; then `run`/`eigenvalues`/`solve`/
  Newton/continuation/… stop it, list `conatus.agent.EXPENSIVE`); Conatus calls that write files
  (`watch`, `output`, `checkpoints`, `save`) are skipped. Not a sandbox: the script's own code (file
  writes, subprocesses) runs with your privileges; never catch `BaseException` around Conatus calls. →
  `ok, calls[{call, line, action}], stopped_at, missing[{call, argument, kind, suggest}],
  refusals[{type, error_code, message, where, why, fix, doc, line}], errors, warnings, explain{model, simulation,
  plan, ...}, plan{type, groups}, memory{peak_bytes (allocators), peak_with_process_floor_bytes (+ the
  declared CUDA context/kernels floor, 512 MiB measured), report} | null, notes,
  validated[{call, values: "checked" | "not checked", checked}], elapsed_s`. `ok` covers what
  `validated` says was checked: the argument values of the stopped call are checked for `run` only.
  Exit 0 ok, 1 refusal/missing/error, 2 usage. Python: `conatus.agent.check(path)`, `conatus.agent.info()`, `conatus.agent.describe(name)`.

## 8. Where the full documentation is

User guide `docs/site/guide/` (geometries, equations, boundary_conditions, timesteppers, gpu, io,
studio_agents, explain, errors, dynamics/*), tutorials `docs/site/tutorials/`, API reference
`docs/site/api/`, frozen surface `python -m conatus._surface`. Web: `/docs/guide/agents.html`.

pages.text:
# Bases and domains

In the expert layer a domain is a coordinate system with one spectral basis per coordinate, each with its size and dealiasing factor.

A `Domain` is a coordinate system and one basis per coordinate. Fourier directions are separable:
the discrete problem splits into independent **groups** (one per wavenumber, or per azimuthal
number $m$ in polar geometry), each solved with banded Olver–Townsend operators.

## Dealiasing factors

Expert-layer bases require an explicit `dealias` factor; there is no default. Native models
select a default and report it in `explain()`.

```python
from conatus.expert import CartesianCoordinates, Chebyshev

z = CartesianCoordinates("z")["z"]
try:
    Chebyshev(z, 32, (-1, 1))
except ValueError as err:
    print(err)
# Chebyshev: dealias must be given explicitly
#   why:   the dealiasing factor sets the grid of the nonlinear products, so the user chooses it
#   fix:   dealias=1 (no padding, linear problems) or dealias=3/2 (quadratic nonlinearities)
try:
    Chebyshev(z, 32, (-1, 1), dealias=True)
except TypeError as err:
    print(err)
# Chebyshev: dealias=True/False is ambiguous; give the factor (1, 3/2, 2, ...)
```

Linear problems (EVP, LBVP) use `dealias=1`; quadratic nonlinearities need `3/2`. The grid size is
`floor(N * dealias)`. With `grid="smooth7"` the grid is raised to the
smallest size whose FFT length has no prime factor larger than 7, so dealiasing stays exact and
the FFTs avoid large-prime lengths:

```python
import numpy as np
from conatus.expert import CartesianCoordinates, RealFourier

x = CartesianCoordinates("x")["x"]
print(RealFourier(x, 170, (0, 2*np.pi), dealias=3/2).grid_size)                  # 255
print(RealFourier(x, 170, (0, 2*np.pi), dealias=3/2, grid="smooth7").grid_size)  # 256
```

The choice is printed by `basis.explain()` and recorded in the provenance and *Methods* text.

## Cartesian bases

| Basis | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `RealFourier(x, N, (a, b), dealias=...)` | real periodic data | cos/sin pairs |
| `ComplexFourier(x, N, (a, b), dealias=...)` | complex periodic data, normal modes | $e^{ikx}$; unknowns declared with `dtype=complex` |
| `Chebyshev(z, N, (a, b), dealias=...)` | bounded interval, walls | $T_n$; tau conditions ({doc}`boundary_conditions`) |
| `Legendre`, `Jacobi(z, N, (a, b), a=, b=, ...)`, `Ultraspherical(..., lam=)`, `ChebyshevU`, `ChebyshevV` | other Jacobi families | sparse operators (Olver–Townsend); taus lifted with `lam=` (below) |
| `MappedChebyshev(y, N, map, dealias=...)` | (semi-)infinite intervals | declared map `TanhMap`, `TanMap`, `RationalMap` |

```python
from conatus.expert import CartesianCoordinates, Chebyshev, MappedChebyshev, TanhMap

z = CartesianCoordinates("z")["z"]
y = CartesianCoordinates("y")["y"]
print(Chebyshev(z, 32, (-1, 1), dealias=3/2).explain())
# Chebyshev(z, size=32, bounds=(-1.0, 1.0), dealias=3/2)
#   family         : Chebyshev T (Jacobi -1/2,-1/2)
#   coefficients   : T_n(t), n = 0..31, t = x
#   dealias        : 3/2 (explicit; grid size 48, floor(N*d))

print(MappedChebyshev(y, 96, TanhMap(L=4.0), dealias=1).explain())
# MappedChebyshev(y, size=96, map=TanhMap(L=4), dealias=1)
#   family         : Chebyshev T in a mapped coordinate
#   coefficients   : T_n(xi), n = 0..95, TanhMap(L=4): y = 0 + 4 artanh(xi), dxi/dy = (1 - xi^2)/4, ...
```

**Legendre, Jacobi and ultraspherical axes.** A wall-bounded axis can be expanded in any Jacobi
family $P_n^{(a,b)}$ ($a, b > -1$; Legendre is $a = b = 0$, $C_n^{(\lambda)}$ the ultraspherical
family, and `ChebyshevU`, `ChebyshevV` are $C^{(1)}$, $C^{(2)}$). An equation of
differential order $q$ is written in the family $P^{(a+q,\,b+q)}$, so its $q$ tau terms are lifted
there: `lift(tau, basis, -1, lam=q)`. Every operator is sparse and exact on the retained modes, the
grid is the Gauss–Jacobi grid of the family, and a non-constant coefficient reports its spectral
tail as on a Chebyshev axis. The checks: Poisson with an exact solution to round-off in each family,
the eigenvalues of a string to $10^{-10}$, and a viscous Burgers run equal to the Chebyshev $T$ run
to $5\times10^{-13}$. In the native layer `cn.walls` is Chebyshev $T$ by default, or a sine/cosine series with
`cn.walls(a, b, basis="sincos")` ({doc}`geometries`); these Jacobi families are
for the expert layer and for scripts imported with `cn.from_dedalus` ({doc}`dedalus`). Their GPU path
(`backend="cuda"`) has run on an A100 only ({doc}`gpu`).

Mapped bases put the resolution where a free shear layer or a critical layer is, without
truncating the line to $[-L, L]$: the Taylor–Goldstein example of the gallery reaches
$J_c = 1/4$ to $2.5\times10^{-12}$ this way. `TanhMap(L, contour=...)` also offers a shifted
complex path. The map and its metric are declared and appear in `explain()`.

The helper `channel(N, base="poiseuille" | "couette" | None)` builds the wall-normal Chebyshev
domain of a plane channel with its base flow as an NCC; everything it chooses is visible in
`ch.explain()` (`dealias=1` by default, since linear problems have no products).

## Curvilinear geometries

The same IR, the same `discretize → plan → eigenvalues / solve / IVPSolver` path; the bases are
regular at the axis or centre. There is no $1/r \to 1/(r+\varepsilon)$ and no condition at
$r = 0$.

| Geometry | Coordinates | Bases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disk | `PolarCoordinates("phi", "r")` | `RealFourier`/`ComplexFourier` × `DiskBasis(r, N, radius, dealias=...)` | Zernike-type $r^{\lvert m\rvert} w(2r^2-1)$ (Vasil et al. 2016) |
| Annulus, Taylor–Couette | `PolarCoordinates` | × `AnnulusBasis(r, N, (ri, ro), dealias=...)` | Chebyshev in $r$, equations multiplied by $r^p$ |
| Pipe, periodic cylinder | `CylindricalCoordinates("phi", "r", "z")` | Fourier × `DiskBasis` × Fourier | Hagen–Poiseuille = Meseguer & Trefethen (2003) |
| Sphere $S^2$ | `S2Coordinates("phi", "theta")` | `RealFourier` × `SphereBasis(theta, N, radius, dealias=...)` | spin-weighted harmonics (Vasil et al. 2019) |
| Shell, ball | `SphericalCoordinates("phi", "theta", "r")` | × `SphereBasis` × `ShellBasis(r, N, (ri, ro), ...)` or `BallBasis(r, N, radius, ...)` | regular at the centre (ball) |

Taylor–Couette and pipe flow are written with these bases in the expert layer (see
{doc}`../tutorials/08_polar`); the native geometries `cn.Annulus` and `cn.Pipe` choose them for
you ({doc}`geometries`).

## Symmetry subspaces

A `SymmetrySubspace(Reflection(z), T=EVEN, ...)` passed to a problem (`symmetry=`) restricts every
field to a declared parity, and each system shrinks to the size of the subspace. Parities are
checked on every equation; an inconsistent declaration is refused. See
{doc}`../tutorials/03_symmetries` and {doc}`dynamics/index`.

## Sine/cosine walls (native layer)

`cn.walls(a, b, basis="sincos")` discretizes a wall axis with sine and cosine series,
$\sin(n\pi(z-a)/L)$ and $\cos(n\pi(z-a)/L)$, $n < N_z$, $L = b - a$. It suits stress-free
walls, fixed-temperature or insulating walls and hinged plates. Each unknown is a pure sine or
cosine series, so its wall conditions hold identically and **no tau term** is needed. The compiler
derives each unknown's parity from its wall conditions and checks that they are consistent:

| Condition (at both walls) | Series |
|---|---|
| `T=0` | sine |
| `"dz(T) = 0"` | cosine |
| `"dz(dz(f)) = 0"` with `f = 0` (hinged) | sine |
| `u=cn.free_slip` (velocity) | tangential components cosine, normal component sine |
| no condition (pressure) | the unique parity that makes every equation equivariant |

The same model text runs with `basis="chebyshev"` (taus) and `basis="sincos"`. Free-slip
Rayleigh–Bénard onset, at $k_c = \pi/\sqrt{2}$, on both sides of $Ra_c = 27\pi^4/4$:

```python
import numpy as np

import conatus as cn

kc = np.pi / np.sqrt(2)                     # critical wavenumber of stress-free RB
Ra_c = 27 * np.pi**4 / 4                    # 657.511...

def model(basis, Ra):
    box = cn.Box(x=cn.periodic(2 * np.pi / kc), z=cn.walls(0, 1, basis=basis))
    m = cn.Model(box, name="RB stress-free", Ra=Ra, Pr=1)
    u, T = m.velocity("u"), m.scalar("T")
    m.pressure("p")
    m.equations("""
        momentum:   dt(u) + grad(p) - Pr*lap(u) - Pr*Ra*T*ez = -u·grad(u)
        continuity: div(u) = 0
        heat:       dt(T) - lap(T) - u·ez = -u·grad(T)
    """)
    m.at("walls", u=cn.free_slip, T=0)      # stress-free, fixed temperature (perturbation)
    return m, u, T

for Ra in (0.99 * Ra_c, 1.01 * Ra_c):
    m, u, T = model("sincos", Ra)
    s = m.linearize(about={u: 0, T: 0}).eigenvalues(8, k=kc, n=1)
    print(f"sincos     Ra/Ra_c = {Ra / Ra_c:.2f}: s = {s.values.real.max():+.15f}")
    m, u, T = model("chebyshev", Ra)
    s = m.linearize(about={u: 0, T: 0}).eigenvalues(16, k=kc)
    print(f"chebyshev  Ra/Ra_c = {Ra / Ra_c:.2f}: s = {s.values.real.max():+.15f}")
```

```text
sincos     Ra/Ra_c = 0.99: s = -0.074208019189859
chebyshev  Ra/Ra_c = 0.99: s = -0.074208019189847
sincos     Ra/Ra_c = 1.01: s = +0.073837897458271
chebyshev  Ra/Ra_c = 1.01: s = +0.073837897458280
```

The closed form $(s/Pr + K^2)(s + K^2)K^2 = Ra\,k^2$, $K^2 = k^2 + \pi^2$, gives
$-0.07420801918986$ and $+0.07383789745827$: the sine/cosine result is exact to round-off (each
group holds one vertical wavenumber, `n=1` selects it; without `n=` all of them are gathered),
the Chebyshev one is spectrally accurate. `m.explain()` declares the choices:

```python
m, u, T = model("sincos", Ra_c)
print("\n".join(l.strip() for l in m.explain(full=True).splitlines() if l.lstrip().startswith(("z:", "u:", "p:", "T:"))))
m, u, T = model("chebyshev", Ra_c)
print("\n".join(l.strip() for l in m.explain(full=True).splitlines() if ("free-slip" in l and "tau" in l) or l.strip().startswith("divergence tau")))
```

```text
z: walls at 0, 1 -> sine/cosine bases (N_z wavenumbers n pi/L, n < N_z, L = 1), realised as the reflection subspace of RealFourier(2 N_z) on [0, 2); no tau
u: cosine/sine by component (x: cosine, z: sine) (free-slip (u·n = 0, dz(u_t) = 0) at walls)
T: sine series (T = 0 at walls)
p: cosine series (deduced from the equivariance of momentum)
```

How it is computed: the axis is the reflection-symmetric subspace (about $z = a$) of a
`RealFourier(2 N_z)` series on the doubled period $[a, 2b - a)$, declared on the IR problem as
`SymmetrySubspace(Reflection(z, about=a), ...)`; plans, eigenvalues and `IVPSolver` run in that
subspace (`reduced=True`, set explicitly; `reduced=False` is refused). The dealiasing factor
applies to the doubled grid. `sim.initial(...)` evaluates your function on $[a, b]$ only and
extends it by the parity (data of a sine field that do not vanish at the walls are refused); `sim.grid(name)` and `sim.coordinate("z")` return the $N_z + 1$ points of $[a, b]$;
`sim.coeffs(name)` and `sim.solver` (expert) keep the doubled-period layout.

What is refused, with what to write instead: a non-homogeneous condition (`T=1` at a wall: write
the perturbation about the conduction profile, or use Chebyshev walls), a Robin or coupled
condition, conditions asking for both a sine and a cosine, no-slip velocity (normal and tangential
components would need opposite parities: use `cn.free_slip` or Chebyshev walls), a coefficient or
base state without parity (`m.given(U=lambda z: 1 - z)`: give it as a cosine/sine series or use
Chebyshev walls), a source term of the wrong parity, and `drift=`. This basis needs no tau
variables, so there are no tau modes to filter; check the spectral convergence of the computed
modes instead.

## Whole line, half line, compound intervals

Three more axes for `cn.Box`, each discretized by a fixed basis printed by `explain()`
(IR: `Hermite`, `Laguerre`, `CompoundChebyshev`):

| Axis | Basis | Conditions | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cn.line(center=0, scale=s)` | Hermite functions $\psi_n((x-x_0)/s)$, Gaussian decay built in | none (no boundary) | `N_x` |
| `cn.half_line(start=0, scale=s)` | Laguerre functions $L_n(y)e^{-y/2}$, $y=(x-a)/s$ | one wall: `"wall"`, `"bottom"`, `"x=a"` | `N_x` |
| `cn.walls(a, c, ..., b)` | Chebyshev $T_n$ on each piece $[a, c], \dots$ | walls at $a$ and $b$; continuity at each $c$ is **automatic** | one size per piece, `N_x=(N_1, N_2, ...)` |

`scale` is required. It is the width of the basis functions, a numerical choice like $N$; choose
it of the order of the width of the solution. On the half line an
equation of order $q$ is written in the derivative basis $L^{(q)}_n e^{-y/2}$ (bidiagonal
derivative and conversions, the Laguerre analogue of the ultraspherical method) and takes $q/2$
conditions at its wall. On a compound interval, for each unknown of order $q$ the value and the
derivatives up to $q-1$ are continuous at every interface; each piece receives $q$ tau terms in
its last modes, and `explain()` lists every one of them.

```python
import numpy as np

import conatus as cn

# whole line: quantum harmonic oscillator, E_n = 2n + 1
m = cn.Model(cn.Box(x=cn.line(scale=1.0)), name="harmonic oscillator")
m.scalar("u")
m.eigenvalue("E", growth="real")
m.given(V=lambda x: x**2)                     # polynomial coefficient: banded, exact
m.equations("E*u + lap(u) - V*u = 0")
E = np.sort(m.eigenvalues(N=40).values.real)
print("E_0..4 =", np.round(E[:5], 12), " max error (n < 20):",
      f"{np.max(abs(E[:20] - (2*np.arange(20) + 1))):.1e}")

# half line: heat equation with u(0) = 0, CNAB2
m = cn.Model(cn.Box(y=cn.half_line(scale=0.5)), name="heat on y >= 0")
m.scalar("u")
m.equations("dt(u) - lap(u) = 0")
m.at("wall", u=0)
exact = lambda y, t: y / (1 + t)**1.5 * np.exp(-y**2 / (4*(1 + t)))
sim = m.simulate(N=40, scheme="CNAB2", dt=1e-3)
sim.initial(u=lambda y: exact(y, 0))
sim.run(until=0.5)
err = np.max(abs(sim.grid("u") - exact(sim.coordinate("y"), sim.t)))
print(f"half line, t = 0.5: max error {err:.1e}")

# compound interval: an interior layer tanh(20 x), same total N = 192
k = 20.0
for label, axis, N in (("walls(-1, 1)", cn.walls(-1, 1), 192),
                       ("walls(-1, -0.15, 0.15, 1)", cn.walls(-1, -0.15, 0.15, 1), (64, 64, 64))):
    m = cn.Model(cn.Box(x=axis), name="layer")
    m.scalar("u")
    m.given(f=lambda x: -2*k*k*np.tanh(k*x) / np.cosh(k*x)**2)
    m.equations("lap(u) = f")
    m.at("bottom", u=np.tanh(-k))
    m.at("top", u=np.tanh(k))
    sol = m.solve(N=N)                        # linear boundary-value model: direct solve
    print(f"{label:>26}: max error {np.max(abs(sol.grid('u') - np.tanh(k*sol.coordinate('x')))):.1e}")
```

```text
E_0..4 = [1. 3. 5. 7. 9.]  max error (n < 20): 2.8e-14
half line, t = 0.5: max error 7.1e-08
              walls(-1, 1): max error 1.3e-07
 walls(-1, -0.15, 0.15, 1): max error 2.5e-14
```

The half-line error is the time error of CNAB2 at `dt = 1e-3` (second order); the spatial error
is below $10^{-9}$ at $N = 40$. What `m.explain(N=(64, 64, 64))` says about the compound layer:

```python
print("\n".join(l.strip() for l in m.explain(N=(64, 64, 64)).splitlines()
                if l.strip().startswith(("x:", "u = ", "u continuous", "dx(u) continuous"))))
```

```text

```

When to use which: a compound interval pays off for a **localized** feature (interior layer,
boundary layer, front); for a smooth solution one interval with the same total $N$ is more
accurate (each piece spends $q$ modes on its taus: $e^x$ on $[-1, 1]$ is $10^{-8}$ with
$(8, 8)$ against $10^{-15}$ with 16). A mapped Chebyshev basis (above) remains the choice for a
bounded but non-decaying solution on an infinite interval; Hermite and Laguerre for decaying ones.

What is refused, with what to write instead: a constant along an unbounded axis (a constant
source, tau or gauge: write the problem for the decaying deviation from the far field), a
non-polynomial coefficient on an unbounded axis (`tanh(x)`: make the term explicit or use a mapped
basis), a condition on `cn.line` (no boundary), one integer for a compound axis
(`N_x=(24, 24)`: one size per piece), incompressible flow on these axes (the gauge/divergence tau
recipe is derived for `walls(a, b)` only: use the IR), symmetry subspaces along them, and the
fused GPU kernel (`f_backend="fused"`: the evaluator runs on the GPU instead, transforms by dense
matrices on the device).

pages.text:
# Boundary conditions

Conditions are declared by boundary name, as on paper; Conatus decides how each one enters the
discrete system and prints that decision.

```python
import conatus as cn

m = cn.Model(cn.Box(x=cn.periodic(2.0), z=cn.walls(-0.5, 0.5)), name="convection", Ra=2500, Pr=1)
u, p, T = m.velocity("u"), m.pressure("p"), m.scalar("T")
m.at("bottom", u=0, T=+0.5)             # no slip, hot plate
m.at("top", u=0, T=-0.5)                # no slip, cold plate

os_ = cn.Model(cn.Box(y=cn.walls(-1, 1)), name="Orr-Sommerfeld", Re=1e4, alpha=1.0)
v = os_.scalar("v")
os_.at("walls", "v = 0", "dy(v) = 0")   # conditions as text, on both walls
```

Keywords set an unknown to a value (a number, or a callable of the boundary's coordinates). Text
conditions accept any equation that involves one unknown at that boundary: derivatives
(`dz(T) = 0`), Robin conditions (`dz(T) + Bi*T = 0`), values given by a parameter. Boundary names
come from the geometry ({doc}`geometries`): `walls` stands for both ends.

## How many conditions

Each unknown needs as many conditions as its order along the bounded coordinate, times the number
of walls divided by two. A temperature with $\nabla^2 T$ between two plates needs two; the
Orr–Sommerfeld equation, fourth order in $y$, needs four (two per wall); in a disk, a ball or a
pipe the centre is not a boundary, so a second-order unknown needs one condition at `wall`.
A pressure that only appears under `grad(p)` needs none: Conatus recognises the incompressibility
structure (below).

A missing condition is refused before anything is built:

```python
import conatus as cn

m = cn.Model(cn.Box(x=cn.walls(0, 1)), name="heat", kappa=1.0)
T = m.scalar("T")
m.equations("dt(T) - kappa*lap(T) = 0")
m.at("x=0", T=0)
try:
    m.simulate(N=16, scheme="SBDF2", dt=1e-3)
except cn.errors.BoundaryConditionError as err:
    print(err)
```

```text
BoundaryConditionError T: 1 boundary condition(s) for 2 needed (order 2 along x, 2 wall(s))
  where: at(...) calls: at('x=0', T = 0)
  why:   missing conditions leave the discrete system singular
  fix:   declare 2 condition(s) on T (boundaries: 'bottom', 'top', 'x=0', 'x=1', 'walls')
```

## What Conatus does with them

Conatus imposes conditions with the tau method: each condition adds one unknown coefficient. It
does not depend on the wall-normal coordinate and may vary along the wall. It enters one equation
multiplied by a fixed polynomial in the wall-normal coordinate. You do not write these terms. They are
placed by one deterministic rule:

- each condition constrains **one** unknown;
- it goes into the equation where that unknown has its **highest order** along the bounded
  coordinate;
- inside that equation, the conditions fill the highest modes in the order you declared them.

`m.explain()` lists every placement:

```text
Boundary conditions -> tau terms (automatic, deterministic):
  T = 0 at walls (left: x=0): tau_T1 lifted into mode N_x-1 of [0] eq0 -- T has its highest x-order (2) there
  T = 0 at walls (right: x=1): tau_T2 lifted into mode N_x-2 of [0] eq0 -- T has its highest x-order (2) there
```

**Incompressibility** is recognised from the structure of the equations, from a divergence
constraint. The pattern is a scalar that appears only under `grad(·)` and has no condition,
paired with the single equation without a time derivative that contains `div(u)`. Conatus then fixes the mean pressure
(`integ(p) = 0`) and adds the divergence correction of the geometry. `m.pressure("p")` only asks
Conatus to check that this structure is there.

## When the rule cannot decide

When the rule cannot decide, Conatus raises an error. Each message names the condition and what to write:

| Situation | What to write |
|---|---|
| the unknown has its highest order in two equations | `m.at(..., into="momentum")`: name the equation that receives the condition |
| a condition involves two unknowns, or none | split it, or write the problem in the {doc}`expert layer <expert>` |
| too many conditions for an unknown | remove one (the extra one would perturb an equation) |
| a scalar condition on one component of a vector unknown | the {doc}`expert layer <expert>`; a stress-free wall is `u=cn.free_slip` (below) |
| an unknown boundary name | one of the names listed by `geometry.boundaries()` |

Writing `lift(...)` yourself in a native model is refused: the placement is Conatus's job, and the
expert layer is there when you want to do it by hand ({doc}`taus`).

## Spurious modes in eigenvalue problems

Truncation creates a few spurious eigenvalues (very large, sometimes unstable). Conatus does not
filter them with a hidden threshold. `m.eigenvalues(N=64, drift=96, drift_tol=1e-6)` solves the problem again
at 96 modes and keeps only the eigenvalues found at both resolutions within the drift tolerance
(yours, required: it decides which modes are returned); the result says how many were removed. A physical filter is allowed, but it is yours and it is logged:
`res.select(np.flatnonzero(abs(res.values) < 2), why="|c| < 2")`. Worked example: {doc}`../tutorials/01_orr_sommerfeld`.

## Free-slip walls in the native layer

In the native layer (`cn.Model`) conditions are written by boundary name and the taus are
placed for you. A stress-free wall is one declaration on the velocity:

```python
import conatus as cn

box = cn.Box(x=cn.periodic(2.0), z=cn.walls(0, 1))
free = cn.Model(box, name="RB stress-free", Ra=700, Pr=1)
u, T = free.velocity("u"), free.scalar("T")
free.at("walls", u=cn.free_slip, T=0)          # u·n = 0 and dz(u_t) = 0 at both walls

rigid = cn.Model(box, name="RB rigid", Ra=2000, Pr=1)
u, T = rigid.velocity("u"), rigid.scalar("T")
rigid.at("walls", u=cn.no_slip, T=0)           # the same as u=0, named for symmetry

slip = cn.Model(box, name="partial slip", nu=1.0)
u = slip.velocity("u")
slip.pressure("p")
slip.equations("dt(u) + grad(p) - nu*lap(u) = -u@grad(u)", "div(u) = 0")
slip.at("bottom", u=cn.navier_slip(0.1))       # u·n = 0, u_t + 0.1 dn(u_t) = 0 (Navier slip length)
slip.at("top", u=cn.no_slip)
slip.simulate(N=(16, 16), scheme="RK443", dt=1e-3).run(steps=2)
```

For a plane wall of normal $n = e_z$ it is compiled as **one vector condition** on the single
unknown $u$,

$$ B(u) = (I - n n)\cdot\partial_z u + n\,(n\cdot u) = 0, $$

whose normal component is $u_z = 0$ and whose tangential components are $\partial_z u_x = 0$
($\partial_z u_y = 0$ in 3D). It therefore reuses the vector-tau rule unchanged: one vector tau per
wall in the equation where $u$ has its highest $z$-order (momentum), and the divergence tau of the
Cartesian recipe in the continuity equation. For the stress-free Rayleigh–Bénard model of
{doc}`bases` (*Sine/cosine walls*):

```python
import numpy as np

import conatus as cn

kc = np.pi / np.sqrt(2)                     # critical wavenumber of stress-free RB
Ra_c = 27 * np.pi**4 / 4                    # 657.511...

def model(basis, Ra):
    box = cn.Box(x=cn.periodic(2 * np.pi / kc), z=cn.walls(0, 1, basis=basis))
    m = cn.Model(box, name="RB stress-free", Ra=Ra, Pr=1)
    u, T = m.velocity("u"), m.scalar("T")
    m.pressure("p")
    m.equations("""
        momentum:   dt(u) + grad(p) - Pr*lap(u) - Pr*Ra*T*ez = -u·grad(u)
        continuity: div(u) = 0
        heat:       dt(T) - lap(T) - u·ez = -u·grad(T)
    """)
    m.at("walls", u=cn.free_slip, T=0)      # stress-free, fixed temperature (perturbation)
    return m, u, T

for Ra in (0.99 * Ra_c, 1.01 * Ra_c):
    m, u, T = model("sincos", Ra)
    s = m.linearize(about={u: 0, T: 0}).eigenvalues(8, k=kc, n=1)
    print(f"sincos     Ra/Ra_c = {Ra / Ra_c:.2f}: s = {s.values.real.max():+.15f}")
    m, u, T = model("chebyshev", Ra)
    s = m.linearize(about={u: 0, T: 0}).eigenvalues(16, k=kc)
    print(f"chebyshev  Ra/Ra_c = {Ra / Ra_c:.2f}: s = {s.values.real.max():+.15f}")
```

`m.explain(full=True)` prints the choices; with Chebyshev walls, the taus are:

```python
m, u, T = model("sincos", Ra_c)
print("\n".join(l.strip() for l in m.explain(full=True).splitlines() if l.lstrip().startswith(("z:", "u:", "p:", "T:"))))
m, u, T = model("chebyshev", Ra_c)
print("\n".join(l.strip() for l in m.explain(full=True).splitlines() if ("free-slip" in l and "tau" in l) or l.strip().startswith("divergence tau")))
```

```text
u: free-slip (u·n = 0, dz(u_t) = 0) at walls (left: z=0): tau_u1 lifted into mode N_z-1 of [0] momentum -- u has its highest z-order (2) there; Chebyshev lift into the last modes
u: free-slip (u·n = 0, dz(u_t) = 0) at walls (right: z=1): tau_u2 lifted into mode N_z-2 of [0] momentum -- u has its highest z-order (2) there; Chebyshev lift into the last modes
divergence tau dot(ez, lift(tau_u2, z, -1)) (the velocity tau of the lowest lifted mode)
```

Validation: the Rayleigh–Bénard onset between stress-free
isothermal walls, $Ra_c = 27\pi^4/4$ at $k_c = \pi/\sqrt{2}$ (Rayleigh 1916; Chandrasekhar 1961),
and the exact growth rate of the mode $n = 1$ to $\sim 10^{-12}$ at $N_z = 16$; the same model
text with `cn.walls(0, 1, basis="sincos")` needs no tau at all ({doc}`bases`, *Sine/cosine
walls*).

On curved walls (disk, annulus, pipe, ball, shell) `m.at("wall", u=cn.free_slip)` (or `"walls"`,
`"inner"`, `"outer"`) means $u_r = 0$ and a vanishing tangential traction,
$r\,\partial_r(u_t/r) = 0$, written without any division by $r$ as one vector condition per wall,
$R\,P_t\cdot\partial_r u + K\cdot u = 0$ with $P_t = I - e_r e_r$ and $K = e_r e_r - P_c$ ($P_c$ projects on
the curved tangential directions; along the pipe axis the condition is $\partial_r u_z = 0$). The
taus are those of no-slip. Checks: a solid-body rotation is
a steady solution (drift $4\times10^{-15}$ in the ball, $2\times10^{-14}$ in the shell over 100 steps,
while no-slip does not even admit it), Stokes decay rates match their Bessel closed forms to
$2\times10^{-12}$ (disk, pipe, ball), $8\times10^{-13}$ (annulus) and $10^{-10}$ (shell). The rank report flags the rigid rotations (groups $\ell=1$ or
$m=0$): a physical kernel, angular momentum is conserved with stress-free walls.

## Interfaces, half lines and the whole line

On a compound interval (`cn.walls(a, c, b)`) you declare the wall conditions only. For each
unknown of order $q$ the native layer adds, at every interface, the continuity of the value and
of the derivatives up to $q-1$, written with one-sided traces, and gives each piece $q$ tau terms
in its last modes; `explain()` lists them (see {doc}`bases`). In the IR the same conditions read

```python
import numpy as np
from conatus.expert import (LBVP, CartesianCoordinates, CompoundChebyshev, Domain, Field, diff,
                            discretize, interp, lap, lift)

cs = CartesianCoordinates("x"); x = cs["x"]
b = CompoundChebyshev(x, (24, 24), (-1, 0.0, 1), dealias=1)     # two pieces, interface x = 0
D = Domain(cs, [b])
u, f = Field("u", D), Field("f", D)
t01, t02, t11, t12 = (Field(name, D.without(x)) for name in ("t01", "t02", "t11", "t12"))
pb = LBVP([u, t01, t02, t11, t12], name="Poisson on two pieces")
pb.add_equation((lap(u) + lift(t01, b, -1, piece=0) + lift(t02, b, -2, piece=0)
                 + lift(t11, b, -1, piece=1) + lift(t12, b, -2, piece=1), f))
pb.add_equation((interp(u, x, 0.0, side="above") - interp(u, x, 0.0, side="below"), 0))
pb.add_equation((interp(diff(u, x), x, 0.0, side="above")
                 - interp(diff(u, x), x, 0.0, side="below"), 0))
pb.add_equation((interp(u, x, "left"), 0))
pb.add_equation((interp(u, x, "right"), 0))
sol = discretize(pb).solve({f: lambda X: -np.pi**2 * np.sin(np.pi * X)})   # u = sin(pi x)
```

and a trace at an interface without `side=` is refused (it is one-sided there). The banded solver
keeps, for each piece, as many pinned columns as that piece has taus (otherwise its banded part
would split into non-square blocks).

`cn.half_line(...)` has one wall (`"wall"`): an equation of order $q$ takes $q/2$ conditions
there, exactly like the radial axis of a disk. `cn.line(...)` has no boundary: a condition on it
is refused (`no boundary`), and so is a trace at $\pm\infty$ in the IR (the Hermite functions
decay; there is nothing to impose).

## Boundary values that depend on time

`t` is the time of a time-dependent model. A boundary value may be any expression of `t`, the
parameters and the given fields, written as text or as a function of `t`:

```python
import numpy as np
import conatus as cn

m = cn.Model(cn.Box(x=cn.periodic(2 * np.pi), z=cn.walls(0, 1)), name="moving walls")
u, T = m.scalar("u"), m.scalar("T")
m.given(S=lambda x: np.sin(x), C=lambda x: np.cos(x))
m.equations("dt(u) - lap(u) = 0", "dt(T) - lap(T) = 0")
m.at("bottom", u="S*cos(t) - C*sin(t)",          # sin(x - t): separable form with given fields
     T="cos(t)")                                 # keyword value as text
m.at("top", "u = 0.5*sin(2*t)",                  # condition text
     T=lambda t: np.exp(-t))                     # numpy functions of t build the expression
m.simulate(N=(16, 16), scheme="RK222", dt=1e-2).run(steps=2)
```

A function of `t` **and** of coordinates (`lambda x, t: np.sin(x - t)`) is refused with the
separable form to write instead: a coordinate itself is not smooth data on a periodic axis. `t` in
an implicit term (`t*u` on the left) or in a model without `dt()` is refused. Such values are
imposed by default with the stage values that the scheme gives for $g'(t)$, exact here
(`bc_time="auto"` → `"rk"`), so that the Runge–Kutta schemes keep their order (RK443 2.8 instead
of 2.0 with $g$ at the stage times). `bc_time="stage"` and `bc_time="step"` are the other
conventions. See {doc}`timesteppers`. In the expert layer the same holds for
`pb.add_bc((interp(u, y, 0), cos(t)))` with `IVPSolver(..., time_parameter="t")`.

On a disk, an annulus, a pipe or a sphere, a given field of the wall coordinate used in a wall
condition (`m.given(g=lambda phi, r: ...)`, `m.at("wall", "T = g")`) is replaced by its trace at the
wall, evaluated from its function (exact, listed by `explain()`); under a derivative (`dr(g)`) it
is refused: declare the wall value as a function of the other coordinates.

pages.text:
# Importing Dedalus scripts

`cn.from_dedalus(script)` builds a Conatus problem from the supported subset of a Dedalus 3 script
and reports translated, approximated and unsupported constructs. It reports, line by line, what it translated. {doc}`../tutorials/14_from_dedalus` goes
through one complete example.

## Usage

The call returns:

- the Conatus problem;
- the declared time stepping;
- the initial and given data;
- a **line-by-line report**.

```python
from pathlib import Path

import conatus as cn

Path("kdv_dedalus.py").write_text("""
import numpy as np
import dedalus.public as d3
period, Nx, damping, dispersion = 8, 64, 3e-4, 5e-4
s = d3.Coordinate('x')
mesh = d3.Distributor(s, dtype=np.float64)
ring = d3.RealFourier(s, size=Nx, bounds=(0, period), dealias=1.5)
h = mesh.Field(name='h', bases=ring)
D = lambda F: d3.Differentiate(F, s)
wave = d3.IVP([h], namespace=locals())
wave.add_equation("dt(h) - damping*D(D(h)) - dispersion*D(D(D(h))) = -h*D(h)")
xs = mesh.local_grid(ring)
h['g'] = np.exp(-2*(xs - 4)**2)
run = wave.build_solver(d3.SBDF3)
run.stop_sim_time = 0.025
dt_fixed = 2.5e-3
while run.proceed:
    run.step(dt_fixed)
""")                                                 # a Dedalus 3 script (KdV-Burgers)

tr = cn.from_dedalus("kdv_dedalus.py")            # a path, or the source text
print(tr.explain())                               # counts + one line per statement
tr.problem                                        # an ordinary Conatus Problem
solver = tr.ivp_solver(startup="lower_order")     # scheme and fixed dt from the script
solver.run(tr.steps())                            # stop_sim_time / dt steps, no Python loop
print(tr.to_script())                             # a runnable program, report as comments
```

In a notebook, `tr` displays the report as a colour-coded table.

## How the script is read

The translator does not execute the script. Python's `ast` module parses it, and a restricted
interpreter walks it statement by statement. It understands:

- literals, arithmetic, tuples and lambdas;
- the `dedalus.public` names it knows;
- a whitelist of NumPy/SciPy functions, used for constants and initial data;
- the equation strings, which go through the {doc}`equations` parser.

Python executes no statement of the script, and the translator does not import Dedalus.

Each statement gets one of four statuses:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **translated** | same mathematics and same method; the note lists any declared rewrite (`trace(grad(u)) -> div(u)`) or default of the source script made explicit (`dealias=1`) |
| **approximated** | translated, but the method differs in a way that can change digits; the note says how |
| **unsupported** | not translated, with the reason and what to write instead; everything that depends on it is reported as well |
| **skipped** | output only: logging, plots, reading results after the solve |

`tr.complete` is true only when a problem was translated with no line unsupported and none
approximated. A time loop whose body changes the simulation (writes field data, calls a mutating
method, stops on a condition) is unsupported, because `solver.run(n)` cannot reproduce it.
`**options` in a call are expanded. A problem's own `namespace={...}` alone resolves the names of
its equations. `tr.to_script()` returns a runnable program. It translates the embedded script
again and refuses to run if a line is unsupported. It then runs the IVP or solves the LBVP. For an
EVP or NLBVP it stops at the discretized plan, because the group or the initial guess is your
choice.

## The translated subset

| Dedalus | Conatus | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `Coordinate`, `CartesianCoordinates`, `PolarCoordinates`, `Distributor(dtype=...)` | coordinate systems; field dtype | process mesh and `comm` are ignored (parallel layout is decided at run time) |
| `RealFourier`, `ChebyshevT`/`Chebyshev`, `Legendre`, `Jacobi(a, b)` | same bases | an omitted `dealias` takes the source default of 1, **written explicitly** |
| `ComplexFourier(N)` | `ComplexFourier(N)` | **approximated**: the source basis keeps the Nyquist mode $k=-N/2$; Conatus drops it, so that group is absent |
| `DiskBasis(coords, shape=(Nphi, Nr))` | `RealFourier`/`ComplexFourier(phi)` × `DiskBasis(r)` | same polynomial space for each $m$ |
| `AnnulusBasis` | × `AnnulusBasis(r)` | **approximated**: Conatus multiplies the equations by a declared power of $r$ |
| `SphereBasis`, `ShellBasis`, `BallBasis`, `S2Coordinates`, `SphericalCoordinates` | — | **unsupported** in the translator: the geometries exist in Conatus ({doc}`geometries`), but the shape-to-size mapping is not automatic |
| `dist.Field`, `VectorField` (named or not) | `Field`, `VectorField` | an unnamed field takes its variable's name (reported) |
| `IVP`, `LBVP`, `EVP(eigenvalue=s)`, `NLBVP`, `IVP(time=t)` | same classes | a 0-dimensional eigenvalue or time field becomes a `Parameter` |
| `add_equation("...")`, `add_equation((lhs, rhs))` | `add_equation` | `u*v` of two tensors is `outer(u, v)` (as in the source language, reported) |
| `Lift(A, basis.derivative_basis(q), n)` | `lift(A, basis, n, lam=q)` | Chebyshev, Legendre, Jacobi, `ChebyshevU/V`, `Ultraspherical` and disk bases (data given in coefficient space on `ChebyshevU/V` is refused: their coefficients are normalised differently) |
| `trace`, `div(ez*lift(tau))` of first-order formulations | `div`, `dot`, `dz` | exact identities, listed in the note |
| `SBDF1-4`, `CNAB1`, `CNAB2`, `MCNAB2`, `CNLF2`, `RK111`, `RK222`, `RK443`, `RKSMR`, `RKGFY` | same schemes, same start-up (lower order first) | time-dependent boundary data: `tr.ivp_solver()` carries them in the explicit part, as the source script does (`bc_time="step"`, said by `explain()`); pass `bc_time="auto"` or `"stage"` to `ivp_solver` for the other conventions ({doc}`timesteppers`); `SBDF2_R`, `RK443_IMEX` are unsupported |
| `solver.step(dt)` in `while solver.proceed` | `solver.run(n)` with fixed `dt` | the time loop becomes one call |
| `CFL(...)`, `compute_timestep()` | — | **unsupported**: Conatus runs with a fixed `dt`; give `dt`, and `conatus.expert.CFL` reports the CFL step |
| `f['g'] = ...`, `f['g'][i] += ...` with grids from `local_grids` | grid functions `tr.data`, used by `set_state` / `ncc` | NumPy/SciPy whitelist |
| `fill_random`, `low_pass_filter`, `f['c'] = ...` | — | **unsupported**: the random layout of the source cannot be reproduced; write an explicit initial condition |
| file handlers, `GlobalFlowProperty` | — | **unsupported**: use `conatus.runs` and the Studio |
| `solve_dense` / `solve_sparse(subproblems[i])` | `eigenvalues(plan, group)` | **approximated**: a subproblem index of the source is not a Conatus group; select the group by wavenumber |

Scripts that build their problem inside a function (for example `rayleigh_benard_evp.py`) are
translated with `from_dedalus(script, entry=("max_growth_rate", dict(Rayleigh=1710, ...)))`.
`overrides={"Nx": 64}` replaces top-level assignments (also a name bound by unpacking, `Nx, Nz = 256, 64`), and each override is listed in the report; an override that matches no top-level assignment is refused with the names that can be overridden.

## Checking a translation

The translator is tested on every official Dedalus 3 example, read unmodified. Six of them were
also run in both forms on a reduced case (smaller sizes, a short time, a deterministic initial
condition, a fixed `dt`): KdV–Burgers, Rayleigh–Bénard, the 2D shear flow, the Poisson problem, the
Rayleigh–Bénard eigenvalue problem and the pipe-flow eigenvalues. The two results agree to
rounding. The spherical examples (sphere, shell, ball) are not translated automatically; write
them as native models ({doc}`geometries`). To check your own translation, run the original script
and the translated problem on a small case and compare one output quantity, as the optional
check script of {doc}`../tutorials/14_from_dedalus` does.
